clue.text: Town house

definitions.meaning: a royal town in Berkshire, west of London, home to a famous castle
the British royal family's dynasty, the reigning house since 1917

explanation.definitionFit: One name serves both a Berkshire town with a royal castle and the dynasty of the present monarchs.

clue.text: This DIY requisite would, we hear, pay

indicators.note: a signal that the preceding word is to be taken by its sound when spoken

parts.note: the clue word itself, said aloud, matches a word for timber
screw is old slang for wages or salary

explanation.surface: A puzzling remark about a handyman's essential being worth paying for.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' turns 'would' into WOOD by sound; SCREW is dated British slang for pay, as in 'a good screw'.
explanation.definitionFit: A threaded fastener for timber is a basic item in any home handyman's toolbox.

clue.text: Church gets money without cuts

indicators.note: used in its old sense of outside, so the money word goes round the church abbreviation

parts.note: banknotes are money

explanation.surface: A church receives funds despite spending cuts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of 'outside', not 'lacking'; 'cuts' is a plural noun, nicks in an edge.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicks or small incisions made in an edge are cuts.

clue.text: It can set off tedious contest

parts.note: something tedious is slow-moving and dull
a match is a sporting contest

explanation.surface: A dull game might be the trigger for something.
explanation.definitionFit: A slow-burning fuse was used to ignite gunpowder, so it can set off a charge.

clue.text: Rebel's leader, liable to be transported

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter, here taken from the rebel

parts.note: apt to and liable to both mean inclined to

explanation.surface: A rebel chief who risks being deported.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transported' looks like shipping off a convict, but it means enraptured.
explanation.definitionFit: To be transported with delight is to be enraptured, completely absorbed.

clue.text: "Can this ——— hold the vasty fields of France?" (Hen V)

definitions.text: "Can this ——— hold the vasty fields of France?" (Hen V)

parts.words: "Can this ——— hold the vasty fields of France?" (Hen V)
parts.note: the missing word from the Chorus's prologue in Shakespeare's Henry V, a scornful name for the small round playhouse

explanation.surface: A quotation from Shakespeare's Henry V with a word left out.
explanation.walkthrough: A fill-in-the-blank: the Chorus apologises that a tiny theatre, likened to a cockfighting ring, must stand for France.
explanation.definitionFit: The word, meaning a small arena for cockfights, is what the Chorus calls the playhouse in that line.

clue.text: Unfading national flag on fleet

parts.note: a nation's colours are its flag
fleet means fast or swift

explanation.surface: A national flag flying over a navy that never loses its brightness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fleet' looks like ships but is the adjective meaning swift; in a down clue 'on' puts the first piece above the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Fabric whose dye will not run or wash out keeps its brightness, so it is unfading.

clue.text: Go carefully through Eastern valley

parts.note: to comb an area is to search it thoroughly

explanation.surface: Searching an eastern valley carefully.
explanation.walkthrough: A COMBE is a short valley or hollow, a word common in southwest English place names.
explanation.definitionFit: A deep, narrow hollow in a hillside is a kind of valley.

clue.text: Old character is upset about current game in India

indicators.note: the Greek letter is placed around the current, enclosing it

parts.note: phi is a letter of the ancient Greek alphabet
AC is alternating current

indicators.note: in a down clue upset turns the word is upside down, so it reads from bottom to top

explanation.surface: An elderly figure is annoyed by the latest Indian pastime.
explanation.walkthrough: PHI goes about AC to give PACHI; 'upset' turns IS into SI.
explanation.definitionFit: This ancient board game played with cowrie shells is the national game of India, ancestor of ludo.

clue.text: Written on the heart of a Spanish gentleman

definitions.text: Written on the heart of a Spanish gentleman

parts.words: Written on the heart of a Spanish gentleman
parts.note: the wavy mark printed over the middle letter n of the Spanish word for sir, señor

explanation.surface: A romantic phrase about something inscribed on a Spaniard's heart.
explanation.walkthrough: The heart is the central letter of SEÑOR, which carries the wavy accent.
explanation.definitionFit: The diacritic that turns n into ñ sits over the central letter of señor.

clue.text: An excuse to perform better

parts.note: an excuse offers a way out, an out
to do is to perform

explanation.surface: Someone looking for a pretext to do a better job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'better' is a verb here, to surpass.
explanation.definitionFit: To surpass someone is to improve on their effort, beating them.

clue.text: East European and Muscovite take line that's controversial

parts.note: a Pole comes from Poland
muscovite is a common variety of the mineral mica

explanation.surface: A Pole and a Russian taking a disputed position.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Muscovite' looks like a Russian, but it is a form of the mineral MICA.
explanation.definitionFit: Polemical writing argues fiercely, so it is contentious and disputed.

clue.text: Engineer making a plan

definitions.meaning: to engineer is to contrive or plot

explanation.definitionFit: As a verb the word means contrive or plot; as a noun it is a programme of action.

clue.text: Reliable cashier, certain to succeed

parts.note: sure means dependable
to cashier is to dismiss, especially from the forces

explanation.surface: A dependable bank clerk who is bound to do well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cashier' is the verb meaning dismiss, not a bank clerk.
explanation.definitionFit: A plan that cannot fail is guaranteed success.

clue.text: Old war once excited dramatist

indicators.note: the letters are stirred up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A past war that once stirred people up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excited' rearranges OLD WAR ONCE.
explanation.definitionFit: The English playwright behind Private Lives and Blithe Spirit was a dramatist.

clue.text: Reduce but feel bitter about giving up nuts at first

indicators.note: the bitter-feeling word gives up a letter, dropping it

parts.note: to resent something is to feel bitter about it

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word nuts

explanation.surface: Someone cutting back while begrudging having to give up nuts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'giving up' removes N, the first letter of 'nuts', from RESENT. 'Reduce' is the medical sense: to set a broken bone back in place.
explanation.definitionFit: In surgery, reducing a fracture means putting bone back into alignment, i.e. setting it again.

clue.text: Insulting attack

explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means rude or giving offence; the noun is a large military assault.

clue.text: Stationery salesman, a favourite, getting acceptable rise

indicators.note: in a down clue rise means the whole string is read upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative
a pet is a favourite
on, as in 'that's not on', means acceptable

explanation.surface: A salesman, a favourite with customers, gets a decent pay rise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rise' turns the whole run REP+A+PET+ON upside down, giving NO TEP A PER.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheets of writing paper are a basic item of stationery.

clue.text: Distressed female, left in at home

indicators.note: upset, so the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A woman in distress, abandoned while staying at home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Distressed' rearranges FEMALE together with L and IN.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase means with one's family, informally, in the domestic setting.

clue.text: Refuses to allow husband to engage in cards

indicators.note: the husband and the engaging word go in the cards word, which surrounds them

parts.note: a card is a witty, amusing person, a wit
to hold someone's attention is to engage it

explanation.surface: A wife forbids her husband from playing at cards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cards' are amusing people, WITS, not playing cards.
explanation.definitionFit: Holding back permission or a payment amounts to declining to grant it.

clue.text: Unexpected turn of events a journalist misrepresented

parts.note: a twist in a story is a surprise development
ED, short for editor, is the usual crossword journalist

explanation.surface: A reporter got a surprise development badly wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: Words that are distorted from their true meaning have been misrepresented.

clue.text: Uncommonly fit, he is a criminal

indicators.note: in an unusual way, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An unusually athletic man turns out to be a crook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uncommonly' rearranges FIT and HE.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who steals is a lawbreaker.

clue.text: Turned a blind eye to negroid evolution

indicators.note: the letters develop into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone dismissing a dated theory of racial evolution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'evolution' rearranges NEGROID.
explanation.definitionFit: To deliberately overlook something is to take no notice of it.

clue.text: Mistake made with a problem — but easily undone

parts.note: a slip is a small error
a knot is a tangled difficulty or problem

explanation.surface: An error compounding a difficulty, though both are simply put right.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is descriptive: a knot that comes apart with one pull.
explanation.definitionFit: This knot is tied so that a tug on one end releases it at once.

clue.text: Make a threatening gesture, say, with old hat

indicators.note: signals that a word is taken by its spoken form

parts.note: to shake one's fist is to make a threatening gesture

explanation.surface: Someone waving a fist while wearing an ancient hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' marks SHAK as sounding like SHAKE, one accepted pronunciation of the hat; O for old follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall cylindrical military cap with a peak and plume is a kind of headgear.

clue.text: The god of love, circumscribing royal destiny

indicators.note: drawing a line around, so the god's name goes round the royal letter

parts.note: Kama is the Hindu god of love
R stands for royal, as in Rex or Regina

explanation.surface: Cupid's counterpart encircling a king's fate.
explanation.walkthrough: KAMA is the Hindu god of desire, the source of the Kama Sutra's name.
explanation.definitionFit: In Hindu and Buddhist thought, the consequences of one's deeds shape one's fate.

clue.text: English naval man, one who followed Falstaff in St Albans, for instance

parts.note: PO is a petty officer, a naval rank
Nym is one of Falstaff's hangers-on in Shakespeare's Henry plays and Merry Wives

explanation.surface: A list of an Englishman, a sailor and one of Falstaff's cronies in an English town.
explanation.walkthrough: St Albans, a cathedral city north of London, takes its name from a person, Saint Alban.
explanation.definitionFit: A name derived from a person, as St Albans is from the martyr Alban.

clue.text: It doesn't fly in over Heathrow

indicators.note: the bird lies inside the words over Heathrow, spanning them

explanation.surface: Something grounded within the flight path over a London airport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' points to letters within 'oveR HEAthrow'. Heathrow is London's main airport.
explanation.definitionFit: This large South American bird, like the ostrich, is flightless.

clue.text: The consequence of working at the farm

indicators.note: the letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: What follows from labouring on the land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' rearranges AT THE FARM.
explanation.definitionFit: The period or result following an event is its outcome.

clue.text: A fairy left in jeopardy

parts.note: a peri is a fairy in Persian mythology

explanation.surface: A fairy abandoned and in danger.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in serious danger is a state of jeopardy.

clue.text: Long established domestic game

parts.note: old means long-standing
a maid is a domestic servant

explanation.surface: A traditional household pastime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'domestic' is a noun, a household servant.
explanation.definitionFit: A simple children's card game in which the loser holds the unpaired queen.

clue.text: Curtail a connection

parts.note: a bridge connects two places

explanation.surface: Cutting a link short.
explanation.definitionFit: To shorten a text by cutting is to curtail it.
